headline: Every major is above its 200-day line, but the tape sold off today anyway
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's cleaner than the price action makes it look. Six of seven majors sit above their 200-day moving average: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, and DOGE. Only ADA sits below, down 76.3% from its 12-month high, the laggard of the group. BNB and ETH carry golden crosses alongside SOL, meaning the 50-day has crossed above the 200-day on those three, a structural trend signal that takes months to build and doesn't erase itself in one red day. Bitcoin itself is 36.5% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81 even after a 21.2% gain over the past month. That gap between 'above trend' and 'well off the high' tells you this is a recovery still in progress, not a market making new highs.

Layer momentum on top and you find a mild disagreement worth naming. RSI readings cluster in the high-50s to high-60s across the board (BTC 63.2, ETH 63.6, SOL 63.3, BNB 67.0), firmly in bullish territory but not yet overbought. Yet BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP all show MACD below signal, meaning short-term momentum is cooling even while the broader RSI reading and the 200-day posture stay constructive. BNB, DOGE, and ADA show MACD above signal, the opposite lean. That's a split tape: some names accelerating on momentum, the largest ones by market cap quietly losing a step. Today's price action fits that: every asset in the set is red on the day, from BTC's -1.4% to SOL's -2.3%, even though the 7-day and 30-day windows are almost uniformly green (BTC +1.8% week, +21.2% month; ADA +8.4% week, +32.7% month). One red day sitting inside a green month is not a trend change, it's a pause, but it's the kind of day that shows up in the RSI and MACD before it shows up in the headline number.

Positioning adds context rather than alarm. Funding rates are cheap across the board: BTC at 0.0028% per 8 hours (3.1% annualized), ETH at 0.0041% (4.5% annualized), SOL barely paying anything at 0.1% annualized. Funding is what longs pay shorts (or vice versa) to hold a perpetual futures position open; low funding means the crowd isn't stretched, which is generally a healthier setup than a market where everyone's paying up to stay long. The exception is the smaller-cap corner: DOGE funding runs 11.0% annualized with a long/short ratio of 3.39, and XRP sits at 6.2% annualized with a 2.47 ratio. Those are crowded books by comparison, and SOL's liquidation data backs it up: $1.27M in long liquidations against just $11,615 in shorts over 9 hours, a lopsided flush that says leveraged longs, not shorts, took the pain today.

The flow picture is where the real tension sits. On the institutional side, BTC spot ETFs posted a net inflow of $174.6M on Sep 4, part of a 5-session net inflow of $986.7M with 3 same-direction days, a real and sustained bid. ETH ETFs added $25.9M on the same day, $215.3M over five sessions. On the whale side, the 72-hour board shows $99.6M net moving off exchanges, all of it concentrated in BTC, with three separate ~$51.5M withdrawals from Coinbase Institutional. Zoom out to the weekly series, though, and the last three full weeks (Aug 18, Aug 25, Sep 01) all show net flows onto exchanges, including a sizable $1,258M onto-exchange week ending Aug 25. Only the most recent week ending Sep 08 flips to $449M net off exchanges. So the immediate 72-hour read and the newest weekly print agree (coins leaving exchanges, generally a sign of holders self-custodying rather than positioning to sell), but that agreement is only one week old against a longer stretch of the opposite. Call it a possible turn, not an established trend. Stablecoin float is up a modest 1.46% over 30 days to $310.6B, dry powder that's growing slowly rather than surging.

Sentiment is the foil here, and it's worth sitting with the mismatch. Fear & Greed reads 69, solidly in Greed territory, near the top of its own 30-day range of 27 to 74. That's a crowd feeling good. But today's tape is red across every major, BTC dominance sits at 59.1%, and total market cap fell 4.01% in 24 hours to $2.68T, a sharper drop than any single major's own daily move, meaning the broader altcoin universe outside this list took a harder hit. Greed at the sentiment gauge sitting alongside a broad daily selloff is the kind of divergence that doesn't resolve itself in the data, it just sits there as a fact to watch.

What to watch from here: whether the off-exchange whale flow becomes a second consecutive weekly print (it would need next week's data to confirm anything beyond one data point), whether BTC and ETH MACD cross back above signal to realign with their still-positive RSI and trend readings, and whether DOGE and XRP funding cool off from their current 11.0% and 6.2% annualized levels or instead build toward the kind of crowded, expensive positioning that tends to precede sharper liquidation events like the one SOL just had.
